opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the warehouses, paying staff and the back office.

follow100Note: Membership fees are only $1.87 of every $100 — but they arrive with almost no cost attached, which is why they cover about two-thirds of the $2.81 Costco kept as profit.
footerNote: Costco's merchandise costs include buying, freight and shrink (lost or damaged goods) — the direct cost of what's on the shelves. The quarter is 12 weeks, ended February 16, 2025.
otherDetail: Interest income and other of $142M, less $36M of interest expense.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in the warehouses and online. Comparable sales rose 6.8% (9.1% adjusted for gas prices and currency).

segments.name: Membership fees
segments.note: Annual membership fees — almost pure profit, and the engine of Costco's earnings.

takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 6.8% across the company (9.1% adjusted for gas prices and currency), and e-commerce sales jumped 20.9% — members kept spending in the warehouses and online.
takeaways.title: Comparable sales still climbing

takeaways.text: Membership fee income rose 7.4% to $1.19B — steady, recurring income with no cost of goods attached to it.
takeaways.title: Membership fees keep growing

takeaways.text: Net income rose to $1.79B ($4.02 per share) from $1.74B a year ago. The small rise understates the quarter: operating income itself rose 12% to $2.32B, but a year ago profit got a $94M tax benefit linked to the special dividend.
takeaways.title: Profit up 2.6% against a tough comparison

verdict: Costco's net sales rose 9.1% to $62.5B as comparable sales climbed 6.8% — and with $1.19B of nearly cost-free membership fees on top, profit rose 2.6% to $1.79B.
